polls.summary: Polls are open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time. A few polling places in the Eastern Time Zone may use Eastern Time. You can't join the line after 7 p.m.
polls.quote: Alabama polling places are open from 7 A.M. to 7 P.M. on Election Day. Please note that polling places located in the Eastern Time Zone may be open from 7 A.M. to 7 P.M. Eastern Time.

id.summary: You must show a photo ID, such as an Alabama driver's license, U.S. passport, or free Photo Voter ID card. Otherwise, two poll workers can vouch for you.
id.quote: A voter who does not have a valid form of photo ID on Election Day can vote a regular ballot only if ... they are positively identified by at least two election officials.

registration.deadline: Monday, October 19, 2026 for online, mail (postmarked by that date), and in-person registration. Online closes at 11:59 p.m.; in person by close of business.
registration.summary: The deadline to register for the November 3 election is October 19, 2026, online, by mail, or in person. Alabama has no same-day or Election Day registration.
registration.quote: Voter registration is open all year, except during the 14 days prior to an election and on Election Day.

selfie.summary: You may take a photo of your own ballot. Taking other photos inside the polling place is not allowed. You may bring a phone if you don't disturb other voters.
selfie.quote: CAN I TAKE PHOTOGRAPHS INSIDE MY POLLING PLACE? Yes. However, an individual may only take a photograph of their own ballot. Taking other photographs within the polling place may intimidate other voters and is not allowed.

AL.notes: Source is the Secretary of State's 2026 Voter Guide PDF; its registration chart lists Oct. 19 for the general election. The ID rule has an exception: two election officials can positively identify a voter who lacks photo ID, so some classifiers call this non-strict. The guide addresses photographing your own ballot but says nothing about sharing it; no ban on sharing was found.

polls.summary: Polls are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Election Day, November 3, 2026.
polls.quote: 11/03/2026 General Election Day. Polls open from 7a.m. – 8p.m.

id.summary: You must show one ID, such as your voter ID card, a driver's license, or a passport. A utility bill or bank statement with your name and address also works.
id.quote: each voter shall exhibit to an election official one form of identification, including (1) an official voter registration card, driver's license, state identification card, current and valid photo identification, birth certificate, passport, or hunting or fishing license

registration.deadline: Sunday, October 4, 2026 (30 days before the election) for online, mail (postmarked), and in-person registration.
registration.summary: The deadline to register or update your registration was October 4, 2026. Alaska does not offer same-day or Election Day registration for state and federal races.
registration.quote: 10/04/2026 Deadline for voters to register to vote or update their registration. Deadline always falls on a Sunday. 30th day prior to the election.

selfie.summary: State law bars you from showing your marked ballot to anyone in a way that reveals how you voted, so sharing a photo of your ballot is not allowed.
selfie.quote: a voter may not exhibit the voter's ballot to an election official or any other person so as to enable any person to ascertain how the voter marked the ballot.

AK.notes: Statute text read via the akleg.gov print view (statutes.asp?media=print&secStart=...). Alaska spans two time zones (the western Aleutians use Hawaii-Aleutian time); the official calendar does not say local time, so the summary omits it. Without ID you may vote a questioned ballot (AS 15.15.225(c)); a poll worker who knows you may waive ID except for first-time mail registrants. AS 15.15.280 does not mention photos specifically; the not_allowed rule is an inference from the ban on exhibiting a marked ballot. Region 4 rural communities have special in-person absentee arrangements.

polls.summary: Polls are open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. If you are in line when polls close, you can still vote.
polls.quote: the polls shall be opened in every precinct at 6:00 a.m. on the day of election and shall be closed at 7:00 p.m.

id.summary: You must show one photo ID with your name and address, such as an Arizona driver license or tribal ID, or two documents like a utility bill and bank statement.
id.quote: A valid form of identification that bears the photograph, name and address of the elector that reasonably appear to be the same as the name and address in the precinct register, including an Arizona driver license

registration.deadline: Monday, October 5, 2026 (registration must be received before midnight of the 29th day before the election), for online, mail, and in-person registration.
registration.summary: Your registration had to be received by midnight on October 5, 2026. Arizona does not offer same-day or Election Day registration.
registration.quote: the registration has been received by the county recorder or the recorder's designee pursuant to section 16-134 before midnight of the twenty-ninth day preceding the date of the election.

selfie.summary: Posting an image of your own ballot isn't a crime, but no one may take photos or videos within 75 feet of a polling place. Mail ballot photos are fine.
selfie.quote: Notwithstanding section 16-1018, a person may not take photographs or videos while within the seventy-five foot limit.

AZ.notes: azsos.gov returned 403 to fetches, so all four answers rest on Arizona Revised Statutes at azleg.gov. Selfie: ARS 16-1018(4) bans showing ANOTHER voter's ballot and says a voter who posts an image of their own ballot consents to retransmittal; ARS 16-515(G) bans photos within the 75-foot limit. Without qualifying ID you vote a provisional or conditional provisional ballot (ARS 16-579). The registration date was computed from the 29-day rule (Nov 3 minus 29 days = Oct 5); azsos.gov could not be checked for a published date. Arizona does not observe daylight saving time, but the Navajo Nation does; the statute does not address time zones.

polls.summary: Polls are open 7:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. If you are in line at 7:30 p.m., you can still vote.
polls.quote: November 3, 2026 – Tuesday GENERAL ELECTION, NONPARTISAN RUNOFF ELECTION, AND ANNUAL SCHOOL RUNOFF ELECTION Polls open 7:30 am to 7:30 pm

id.summary: You must show a photo ID, such as an Arkansas driver's license or U.S. passport. Without one, you vote provisionally and must show ID by the following Monday.
id.quote: Provisional ID - If you voted provisional because of not having sufficient identification, you will have until the Monday after the election to provide identification to the County Clerkto have your vote counted

registration.deadline: Monday, October 5, 2026 (the 30-day deadline falls on Sunday, October 4, and moves to the next business day).
registration.summary: The deadline to register for the November 3 election was October 5, 2026. Arkansas does not offer same-day or Election Day registration.
registration.quote: October 4, 2026 – Sunday* 30 DAYS PRIOR TO THE GENERAL ELECTION Deadline to apply to register to vote in the General Election. ... The actual deadline will be Monday, October 5, 2026.

AR.notes: Accepted IDs are listed in the State Board of Election Commissioners' 2026 Poll Worker Guide (sbec.arkansas.gov): AR driver's license or ID (including the Mobile ID app), concealed carry license, U.S. passport, military ID, college ID; may be expired up to 4 years. The poll worker guide says provisional ID voters can return 'before Monday at noon following the election'; the SOS page says 'until the Monday after the election.' Selfie: no Arkansas statute or official guidance found on ballot photos; the official code site is LexisNexis and could not be searched. The SOS pages offer only paper registration forms; I did not find an online registration option, but did not confirm in writing that none exists. 'No same-day registration' rests on the 30-day deadline in Ark. Code 7-5-201(a) and Amendment 51.

polls.summary: Every voter gets a mail ballot. Polls and vote centers are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. on November 3. Drop off your ballot by 8 p.m., or mail it postmarked by November 3.
polls.quote: November 3 is the last day to vote in-person or return a ballot by 8:00 p.m. Polls are open from 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.

id.summary: Most voters don't need to show ID. Some first-time voters who registered by mail or online without an ID number may be asked for a license, passport, or utility bill.
id.quote: Do I Need to Show ID to Vote in California? In most cases, NO. California does not generally require voters to show identification at the polls.

registration.deadline: Monday, October 19, 2026 to register online (the standard 15-day deadline). After that, Same Day Voter Registration (Conditional Voter Registration) is available at county elections offices, vote centers, and polling places through Election Day.
registration.summary: The regular deadline is October 19, 2026. After that, you can still register and vote the same day at your county elections office, a vote center, or a polling place.
registration.quote: Eligible citizens who need to register or re-register to vote within 14 days of an election can complete this process to register and vote at their county elections office, polling place, or vote center.

selfie.summary: Since 2017, state law lets you photograph your own ballot and share it. Poll workers can still respond if photos disrupt voting, and you can't photograph voters entering or leaving.
selfie.quote: A voter may now take a photograph of their ballot (a “ballot selfie”) and share it on social media.

CA.notes: Deadline quote for Oct. 19 is on the SOS Nov. 3, 2026 page: 'The last day to register to vote online for November 3, 2026, General Election is October 19.' Mailed ballots must be postmarked by Nov. 3 and received within 7 days (SOS Where and How to Vote page). The ID page used is the SOS 2026 primary Voter Information Guide archive; the current-guide URL returned 403. Selfie source is SOS County Clerk memo #17014 (Feb. 2017) quoting Elections Code 14291(b) as amended by AB 1494; leginfo.legislature.ca.gov blocked fetching, so the code text was read through the memo. Elections Code 18541 bars photographing voters entering or exiting a polling place within 100 feet.

polls.summary: Colorado votes by mail. Your ballot must reach your county clerk by 7 p.m. on November 3; postmarks don't count. Voter service and polling centers are open for in-person voting until 7 p.m.
polls.quote: Postmarks do not count; ballots must be in the hands of the county clerk by 7:00 PM on Election Day in order to be counted.

id.summary: If you vote in person, you must show ID. Most voters use a Colorado driver's license or Colorado ID, but many other forms are accepted.
id.quote: All voters who vote in-person must provide identification. While there are many forms of acceptable identification, most voters find it convenient to bring their Colorado driver's license or Colorado ID.

registration.deadline: Monday, October 26, 2026 (8th day before Election Day) to register online or by mail and still get a ballot by mail. After that, register in person at a voter service and polling center through Election Day.
registration.summary: Register online or by mail by October 26, 2026 to get a mail ballot. After that, you can register and vote in person at a voter service and polling center through Election Day.
registration.quote: If you miss the above deadlines, you may register in-person at a voter service and polling center in your county through Election Day.

selfie.summary: A 2017 law lets you show your voted ballot to others and share a photo of it. County clerks may set reasonable limits on photography at voting centers.
selfie.quote: any voter may show his or her voted ballot to any other person

CO.notes: Colorado runs all-mail elections, so 'open' is null: the FAQ gives the 7 p.m. deadline but no opening time for voter service and polling centers on Election Day, and opening hours vary by county. The Oct. 26 date is computed from 'through the 8th day before Election Day' (Nov. 3 minus 8 days); the FAQ gives the rule, not the date. Selfie: HB17-1014 (signed March 16, 2017, effective Aug. 9, 2017) removed the ban on showing a voted ballot; the quote comes from the bill summary on leg.colorado.gov, read through WebFetch.

polls.summary: Polls are open 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. If you are in line by 8 p.m., you can vote. Same-day registration locations keep the same hours.
polls.quote: Polls are open 6 a.m. – 8 p.m. • As long as you’re in line by 8 p.m., you can vote, and your vote will be counted.

id.summary: You'll be asked for a Social Security card or any preprinted ID showing your name plus your address, signature, or photo. If you have none, you can sign a statement.
id.quote: Social security card or any pre-printed form of ID showing the voter’s name together with his or her (1) address, (2) signature, or (3) photograph Alternative to ID Sign a statement on Form ED-681

registration.deadline: Friday, October 16, 2026 for in-person (registrar of voters, until 8 p.m.), mail (postmarked), and online (by 11:59 p.m.). After that, Same Day Registration during early voting (October 19 to November 1) and on Election Day at your town's designated location.
registration.summary: The regular deadline was October 16, 2026. You can still register and vote the same day during early voting, October 19 to November 1, or on Election Day at your town's Same Day Registration location.
registration.quote: If you miss the October 16 voter registration deadline, you can still register and vote through Same Day Registration. Same Day Registration is available: • During all Early Voting hours (October 19 – November 1) • On Election Day

CT.notes: Changed recently: P.A. 23-5 (effective Jan. 1, 2024) moved the regular registration deadline from 7 days to 18 days before the election and added same-day registration during early voting. ID: an affidavit (Form ED-681) is accepted instead of ID, so this is arguably closer to 'ID requested'; first-time voters who registered by mail without ID verification must show photo ID or a document with name and address. Selfie: the 2026 SOTS Voter Guide only says media may not photograph how a voter marks a ballot; no statute or SOTS guidance on voters photographing their own ballots was found in CGS Title 9 chapters 143 to 157. Hours: CGS 9-174 (chapter 146) also sets 6 a.m. to 8 p.m.

polls.summary: Polls are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. You must vote at your assigned polling place on Election Day.
polls.quote: Voters must vote at their assigned Polling Place on Election Day. Polls are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.

id.summary: You must show proof of identity, such as a photo ID, utility bill, or bank statement. If you don't have it with you, you can sign an affidavit and vote.
id.quote: In the event the voter does not have proof of identity with them, the voter shall sign an affidavit of affirmation that the voter is the person listed on the election district record.

registration.deadline: Saturday, October 10, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. (4th Saturday before the election). Mailed applications postmarked by the deadline count.
registration.summary: The deadline to register for the November 3 election was October 10, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Delaware does not currently offer same-day or Election Day registration.
registration.quote: The 2026 General Election Voter Registration Deadline is Saturday, October 10, 2026, at 11:59 p.m.

DE.notes: Changed recently: the Delaware Supreme Court struck down the 2022 same-day registration law in 2024 (Albence v. Higgin), so 'no' reflects current practice; the Department page gives only the Oct. 10 deadline and doesn't mention same-day registration. ID: 15 Del. C. 4937(a) requires 'proof of identity' with an affidavit alternative; the accepted-document list (photo ID, utility bill, bank statement, government check) is quoted on the Department's provisional ballot page. Selfie: no Title 15 provision on voters photographing or showing their ballot was found; Title 15 only tells election officers to make sure no mirror or camera can view the ballot. Registration quote was read at elections.delaware.gov/voter/votereg.shtml (the site's nav links to votereg.html).

polls.summary: Every voter is mailed a ballot. On November 3, vote centers are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m., and you can use any one. Mailed ballots must be postmarked by November 3.
polls.quote: 2026 General Election Day Vote Centers Tuesday, November 3, 2026, from 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Voters may cast their ballots AT ANY VOTE CENTER regardless of their residential address

id.summary: Most voters don't show ID. If you first registered by mail or online, you may need ID with your name and address, like a photo ID or utility bill.
id.quote: If you are registering to vote in the District of Columbia for the first time and submit a voter registration application by mail or electronically, you may be required to provide identification that shows your name and current address

registration.deadline: Tuesday, October 13, 2026 (21 days before the election) for online and mail applications to be received. After that, register in person with proof of residence at an Early Vote Center or an Election Day Vote Center.
registration.summary: Online and mail registrations had to arrive by October 13, 2026. You can still register and vote the same day during early voting or on Election Day if you bring proof of residence.
registration.quote: On Election Day, between the hours of 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m., qualified electors may register to vote and cast full ballots in person at Vote Centers.

DC.notes: The 2026 General Election Calendar (Rev. 10/1/2026) lists Oct. 13 as the 'Deadline for receipt of all voter registration applications ... except for those submitted in person at the Board or at voter registration agencies (21 days before the election)'. Mailed ballots must be postmarked by Election Day and received by Nov. 13, 2026. Selfie: no DC Code, DCMR, or DCBOE statement found; news reports quote a DCBOE spokesperson saying there is no ban, but that is not an official source.

polls.summary: Polls are open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time (Florida has two time zones). If you are in line at closing, you can vote.
polls.quote: The polls shall be open at the voting places at 7:00 a.m., on the day of the election, and shall be kept open until 7:00 p.m., of the same day

id.summary: You must show a current photo ID with your signature, such as a Florida driver license, Florida ID card, or U.S. passport. Without one, you vote a provisional ballot.
id.quote: The clerk or inspector shall require each elector, upon entering the polling place, to present one of the following current and valid picture identifications: 1. Florida driver license.

registration.deadline: Monday, October 5, 2026 (29 days before the election).
registration.summary: The deadline to register for the November 3 election was October 5, 2026. Florida does not offer same-day or Election Day registration.
registration.quote: Deadline to register to vote: October 5, 2026

selfie.summary: You may photograph your own ballot. No other photography is allowed in the polling room or early voting area.
selfie.quote: No photography is permitted in the polling room or early voting area, except an elector may photograph his or her own ballot.

FL.notes: ID: Fla. Stat. 101.043 lists accepted photo IDs; if the photo ID lacks a signature, a second ID with a signature is required. The accepted-ID list was amended in recent sessions, so the statute site (leg.state.fl.us, current-year statutes) is the place to recheck. Fla. Stat. 102.031(5) permits photographing your own ballot; it does not separately address sharing it, and no ban on sharing was found. 'No same-day registration' rests on the 29-day deadline on the DOS registration page.

polls.summary: Most polling places are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. A polling place with fewer than 400 voters may open as late as noon, and the county mails a notice if it does.
polls.quote: Except as provided in subsections (2)(a) and (3), polling places must be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.

id.summary: You must show a photo ID, such as a Montana driver's license, U.S. passport, or tribal photo ID. Other photo IDs count when paired with a utility bill or bank statement.
id.quote: a current utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, government check, or other government document that shows the elector's name and current address; and (B) photo identification that shows the elector's name.

registration.deadline: Regular registration closed October 5, 2026 (mail postmarked by then is accepted). Late registration at your county election office runs from October 6 through noon on Election Day, November 3, 2026.
registration.summary: Regular registration closed October 5. You can still register late at your county election office and vote there, up to noon on Election Day.
registration.quote: In a federal election, an elector may register or change the elector's voter registration information after the close of regular registration ... (c) prior to noon on the day of the election.

selfie.summary: Montana's Commissioner of Political Practices says taking a selfie with your own marked ballot and sharing it does not break state law.
selfie.quote: Voluntarily taking a picture of yourself (a “selfie”) with your marked ballot and sharing the image on social media or with family and friends does not violate the prohibitions of Mont. Code Ann.§ 13-35-201.

MT.notes: 2025 law (Ch. 409) moved the Election Day late-registration cutoff to noon. SB 490 Saturday registration is blocked by court order per votemt.gov. sosmt.gov returned 403; statutes used. Selfie source is a 2018 advisory opinion (COPP), not a statute; polling-place photo policy beyond that not found. Online registration options were not checked.

polls.summary: Nebraska spans two time zones. Polls are open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. in the Central Time Zone and 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. in the Mountain Time Zone.
polls.quote: The polls are open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. in the Central Time Zone and from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. in the Mountain Time Zone.

id.summary: You must show a photo ID with your name and photo, such as a Nebraska driver's license, state ID, or U.S. passport. Expired IDs work. Without one, you vote provisionally.
id.quote: Yes, voters must present an acceptable form of photo ID before casting a ballot in every primary, general and special election.

registration.deadline: Online by midnight and mail postmarked by Friday, October 16, 2026. In person at your county election office by 6 p.m. Friday, October 23, 2026.
registration.summary: Register online or by mail by October 16, or in person at your county election office by 6 p.m. October 23. Nebraska has no Election Day registration.
registration.quote: 23-Oct At 6 PM - last day for in-person voter registration. §32-302

selfie.summary: State law lets you photograph your own marked ballot and share the photo. No one may pressure you to show your ballot.
selfie.quote: This subsection does not prohibit a voter from voluntarily photographing his or her ballot after it is marked and revealing such photograph in a manner that allows the photograph to be viewed by another person.

NE.notes: Photo ID law LB514 took effect May 2024. Voters with a reasonable impediment can sign a certification and vote provisionally; provisional voters without ID can show ID at the county office by the Tuesday after the election. Election Day registration not offered (only presidential-only ballots for recent movers in presidential years). Polling-place photo policy beyond 32-1527 not found.

polls.summary: Nevada mails a ballot to active voters, and in-person polling places are also open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Election Day. Return a mail ballot by hand or drop box before polls close, or mail it postmarked by Election Day so it arrives by 5 p.m. on the fourth day after.
polls.quote: at all elections held under the provisions of this title, the polls must open at 7 a.m. and close at 7 p.m.

id.summary: Most registered voters do not show ID; you sign to vote. Some first-time voters who registered by mail or online must show a photo ID or a utility bill.
id.quote: May vote at a polling place only if the person presents to the election board officer at the polling place: (1) A current and valid photo identification of the person

registration.deadline: Mail and in person at the county clerk: Tuesday, October 6, 2026. Online: through Election Day, November 3, 2026. You can also register in person at an early voting site or at your polling place on Election Day.
registration.summary: Register by mail or at the county clerk by October 6, or online through Election Day. You can also register and vote in person during early voting or on Election Day.
registration.quote: an elector may register to vote in person on the day of the election at any polling place in the county or city, as applicable, in which the elector is eligible to vote.

selfie.summary: State law bars members of the public from photographing voting at a polling place. No state law found that addresses photos of your own mail ballot.
selfie.quote: A member of the general public shall not photograph the conduct of voting at a polling place or record the conduct of voting on audiotape or any other means of sound or video reproduction.

NV.notes: nvsos.gov blocked automated fetching (Incapsula), so all four answers come from NRS chapter 293 (page includes 2025 amendments). Mail ballot return quote is NRS 293.269921; registration deadlines NRS 293.560 (mail/in person fourth Tuesday before = Oct 6; online through Election Day). Voter ID: Question 7 (2024) passed once and is on the Nov 2026 ballot for a second vote; AB 499 (2025) was vetoed, so no ID rule applies for this election. Selfie rule is an inference from NRS 293.274; whether it applies to a voter's own ballot is not stated; SOS FAQ could not be checked.

polls.open: No later than 11 a.m. (varies by town)
polls.close: No earlier than 7 p.m. (varies by town)
polls.summary: Hours vary by town and city. Polls must open by 11 a.m. and stay open until at least 7 p.m.; many open earlier. Check your town or city clerk for exact hours.
polls.quote: At all state elections in towns and cities the polls shall open not later than 11 o'clock in the morning and shall close not earlier than 7 o'clock in the evening.

id.summary: You must show a valid photo ID, such as a driver's license, state ID card, military ID, or U.S. passport. Without one, an election official must verify who you are.
id.quote: If the supervisor of the checklist determines that the voter's qualifications and identity have not been established, the voter shall not be allowed to vote.

registration.deadline: Register with your town or city clerk before the supervisors of the checklist's last session, held 6 to 13 days before the election (about October 21 to 28, 2026, set by each town). You can also register at your polling place on Election Day, November 3, 2026.
registration.summary: Register with your town or city clerk before the last checklist session, 6 to 13 days before the election, or at your polling place on Election Day. You must bring proof of citizenship.
registration.quote: Any person whose name is not on the checklist but who is otherwise a qualified voter shall be entitled to vote by requesting to be registered to vote at the polling place on election day.

NH.notes: sos.nh.gov blocks automated fetching (Akamai 403), so answers use RSA text. ID: 2024 law (Ch. 378, eff. Nov 11, 2024) removed the affidavit options; as of Sept 8, 2026 an official who personally knows you can attest to your identity. Registration now requires proof of citizenship (RSA 654:12), e.g., birth certificate, passport, or naturalization papers. Selfie: RSA 659:35 still says a voter may not photograph and share a marked ballot, but the First Circuit struck that ban down in Rideout v. Gardner (2016); no official SOS page confirming current enforcement was reachable, so left null. Do not publish 'not allowed' from the statute text alone.

polls.summary: Polls are open 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Election Day, November 3, 2026. In-person early voting runs October 24 to November 1.
polls.quote: 11/03/26 General Election Day Polls Are Open From 6 A.M. - 8 P.M.

id.summary: Most voters do not show ID. Some first-time voters who registered by mail must show ID, such as a driver's license or utility bill, or vote provisionally.
id.quote: If you DO NOT show the board workers any identification you CANNOT vote on the voting machine. You MUST vote with a provisional paper ballot.

registration.deadline: October 13, 2026 (21 days before the election), online, by mail, or in person.
registration.summary: The deadline to register for the November 3 election was October 13, 2026. New Jersey does not offer Election Day registration.
registration.quote: The Voter Registration Deadline is 21 days before the election. General Election – October 13, 2026

selfie.summary: State law says no one may show their ballot inside the polling room. No law found that addresses photos of a mail ballot at home.
selfie.quote: NJSA 19:34-7 Violation of ballot regulations No person shall within the polling room mark his ballot in a place other than in the polling booth or show his ballot

NJ.notes: ID quote applies only to 'Need ID' voters listed on the poster (mail registrants after 2003 who never voted federally in the county, or whose numbers were not verified). Selfie: 19:34-7 bans showing a ballot in the polling room; news reports describe ballot selfies as illegal in NJ, and bills to allow them have stalled. No Division of Elections FAQ on selfies found.

polls.summary: Polling locations are open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Election Day. Mailed ballots must be received by 7 p.m. on Election Day.
polls.quote: Polling locations will be open from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. Check with your County Clerk for location information. Mailed ballots must be received by 7:00 p.m.

id.summary: Most voters do not show ID; you state your name, year of birth, and address. First-time voters who registered by mail without ID must show one.
id.quote: Otherwise, you will be asked to provide a verbal or written statement of identification including your name, year of birth, and registered address.

registration.deadline: Mail, agent, and online registration closed October 6, 2026 (28 days before). Same-day registration is available in person during early voting and at any polling location in your county on Election Day, November 3, 2026.
registration.summary: Regular registration closed October 6. You can still register and vote the same day at your County Clerk's office, some early voting sites, or any polling location in your county on Election Day.
registration.quote: Any eligible voter in New Mexico can register to vote or update their voter registration and then vote on the same day at their County Clerk’s office or at any polling location in their county on Election Day

NM.notes: Same-day registration requires a physical ID (government, tribal, or school photo ID; plus a recent document if the address differs). The SOS voter registration FAQ still says late applications are held until after the election, which predates same-day registration; the SDR FAQ and the 2026 dates sheet both confirm Election Day SDR. The Oct 6 date comes from the 28-day rule and the SOS candidate guide summary; the dates PDF lost its date graphics in text extraction. Selfie: no official SOS or statute text found; news reports conflict (2016 'technically illegal', 2020 'allowed').

polls.summary: Polls are open 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. on Election Day, November 3, 2026. Early voting runs October 24 to November 1, with hours set by each county.
polls.quote: the general election from six o’clock in the morning until nine o’clock in the evening

id.summary: Most voters do not show ID. Some first-time voters who registered by mail must show a photo ID, utility bill, bank statement, or paycheck.
id.quote: presents to the appropriate election inspector, clerk or coordinator a current and valid photo identification; or ( ii ) presents ... a copy of a current utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck

registration.deadline: Your application must be received by your county board of elections by October 24, 2026. Address changes are due October 19.
registration.summary: Your registration must reach your county board of elections by October 24, 2026. New York does not offer Election Day registration.
registration.quote: Oct 24 Registration Deadline for General Election: Last day application must be received by BOE to be eligible to vote in General Election.

selfie.summary: State law bars showing your marked ballot to anyone in a way that reveals your votes, which covers ballot selfies. A federal court upheld the ban at polling places.
selfie.quote: 10. Shows his ballot after it is prepared for voting, to any person so as to reveal the contents, or solicits a voter to show the same

NY.notes: elections.ny.gov blocks curl/WebFetch (403); pages and PDFs were read in Chrome. Election Law compilation is amended through Laws 2025, ch. 701. Registration deadline moved to 10 days before the election by 2022 law. ID quote is Election Law 8-303 (HAVA first-time mail registrants). Selfie: Election Law 17-130(10); Silberberg v. Board of Elections (S.D.N.Y. 2017) upheld the ban at polling sites. Whether BOE enforces it against mail-ballot photos is not stated; treat as not allowed per statute text. Section 17-130 is headed 'Misdemeanor in relation to elections.'

polls.summary: Polling places are open 6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. on Election Day. If you are in line at 7:30 p.m., you can still vote.
polls.quote: Polling places will be open from 6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. on Election Day. Any voter in line at their assigned polling place at 7:30 p.m. will be able to vote.

id.summary: You will be asked for a photo ID, such as a NC driver's license, U.S. passport, or free voter ID card. Without one, you can fill out an ID Exception Form.
id.quote: If a voter cannot show an acceptable photo ID when voting in person, they can still vote by filling out an ID Exception Form.

registration.deadline: Friday, October 9, 2026 (25 days before Election Day). After that, you can register and vote the same day only at an early voting site during the early voting period.
registration.summary: The regular deadline is October 9, 2026. After that, you can register and vote at the same time during early voting, but not on Election Day.
registration.quote: If you missed the voter registration deadline, you may still be able to register and vote or make changes (except for party affiliation) to your voter registration and vote during the early voting period.

selfie.summary: State law bars photographing a voted ballot. It also bars photographing voters inside the voting area without permission from the voter and the chief judge.
selfie.quote: No person shall photograph, videotape, or otherwise record the image of a voted official ballot for any purpose not otherwise permitted under law.

NC.notes: Photo ID enforced since 2024. With an ID Exception Form you vote provisionally, and county boards must count it if the form is truthfully completed. October 9 is computed from the 25-day rule on the SBE page (25 days before Nov 3 is Oct 9). G.S. 163-166.3(c) has no exception for your own ballot.

polls.open: Between 7 a.m. and 9 a.m. local time (set by county or city)
polls.close: Between 7 p.m. and 9 p.m. local time (set by county or city)
polls.summary: Hours vary by county or city. Polls open by 9 a.m. (no earlier than 7 a.m.) and stay open until at least 7 p.m. (no later than 9 p.m.) local time. North Dakota spans two time zones.
polls.quote: The polls at all primary, general, and special elections must be opened at nine a.m. or earlier, but not earlier than seven a.m.

id.summary: You must show a North Dakota driver's license, nondriver ID, or tribal ID with your name, current address, and birth date. A utility bill can fill in missing details.
id.quote: A qualified elector shall provide a valid form of identification to the proper election official before receiving a ballot for voting.

registration.deadline: No deadline. North Dakota has no voter registration; bring a valid ID showing your current residential address.
registration.summary: North Dakota has no voter registration. If you are eligible, you can vote on Election Day by showing a valid ID with your current address.
registration.quote: North Dakota does not require voter registration, but you do need to have a valid form of identification that can be used for voting.

ND.notes: No voter registration exists, so 'yes' is used for registration rule because eligible residents can vote on Election Day with ID; the page may want custom wording. ID: without valid ID you mark a set-aside ballot and must show ID within 13 days (before the canvassing board meets), per sos.nd.gov. The ID types do not have to carry a photo by statute (tribal IDs/letters, long-term care certificates), so classed id_nonphoto; it is stricter than most nonphoto states because supplemental documents only fill gaps in a listed ID. Selfie: no provision found in NDCC chapters 16.1-01, -05, -13, or -15, and no SOS guidance found.

polls.summary: On Election Day, polls are open 6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. You must vote at your assigned precinct polling place.
polls.quote: On Election Day, you must cast your ballot in your precinct at your designated polling place between the hours of 6:30 a.m. and 7:30 p.m.

id.summary: You must show an unexpired photo ID, such as an Ohio driver's license, state ID card, U.S. passport, or military ID. Without one, you vote a provisional ballot.
id.quote: Ohio law requires voters to present a valid, unexpired photo ID that includes their name and photograph.

registration.deadline: Monday, October 5, 2026 (30 days before; the 30th day falls on a Sunday, so the deadline moves to the next business day). Mail forms must be received or postmarked by then.
registration.summary: The deadline was October 5, 2026, online, by mail, or in person. Ohio has no same-day or Election Day registration.
registration.quote: Ohio law requires registration at least 30 days before an election. If the deadline falls on a Sunday or legal holiday, it extends to the next business day.

selfie.summary: State law bars letting others see your ballot to show how you are about to vote. No official guidance was found on sharing a ballot photo after voting.
selfie.quote: being an elector, allow the elector's ballot to be seen by another, except as provided by section 3505.24 of the Revised Code, with the apparent intention of letting it be known how the elector is about to vote

OH.notes: ohiosos.gov blocks curl (403); read in Chrome. Photo ID law HB 458 took effect April 2023; provisional voters without ID must show ID at the board of elections within four days (not quoted from the page). Oct 5 is computed from the 30-day rule. Selfie: R.C. 3599.20 wording is about a ballot 'about to' be voted; whether it reaches a post-voting selfie is unclear, and no SOS FAQ addresses it. Consider null if 'limited' overstates it.

polls.summary: Polls are open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Election Day.
polls.quote: The polls are open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.

id.summary: Show a current photo ID, such as a driver's license, or the free voter ID card your county election board mailed you. Without either, sign an affidavit and vote provisionally.
id.quote: In addition, voters may use the free voter identification card they received by mail from the County Election Board when they registered to vote.

registration.deadline: Applications must be postmarked or delivered by Friday, October 9, 2026 (25 days before the election).
registration.summary: Your application must be postmarked by October 9, 2026. Registration then closes until after the election; Oklahoma has no Election Day registration.
registration.quote: Voter registration is closed for 24 days prior to an election. Applications must be postmarked no later than 25 days prior to the election.

selfie.summary: You may take a picture of your marked ballot, but do not post or share it until you are outside the election enclosure, where you check in and vote.
selfie.quote: Feel free to take a picture of your marked ballot – but don’t post your picture to social media or share it with anyone until you are outside of the election enclosure.

OK.notes: Oct 9 is computed from the 25-day rule. The OK Voter Portal says you can register or update registration there. Selfie guidance adds that disclosing your vote inside the election enclosure is a crime.

polls.summary: Polls are open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. at your assigned polling place. If you are in line by 7 p.m., you can still vote.
polls.quote: You can vote in person on Election Day from 7 a.m. until 7 p.m. at your assigned polling place. If you are in line by 7 p.m., you will still be allowed to vote.

id.summary: You must show a photo ID, such as a Georgia driver's license (even if expired), a U.S. passport, or a free Georgia voter ID card from your county registrar.
id.quote: Georgia law requires photo identification when voting, either in person or absentee.

registration.deadline: Monday, October 5, 2026 for the November 3 general election.
registration.summary: The deadline to register for the November 3 election was October 5, 2026. Georgia does not offer same-day or Election Day registration.
registration.quote: General Election/Special Election 11/03/2026 October 13 – October 30 10/05/2026

selfie.summary: State law bars using cameras or cell phones in a polling place while voting is going on, unless a poll manager allows it. Mail ballots are not addressed.
selfie.quote: O.C.G.A. §21-2-413: (e) No person shall use photographic or other electronic monitoring or recording devices, cameras, or cellular telephones while such person is in a polling place while voting is taking place

GA.notes: sos.ga.gov blocks curl and WebFetch (Cloudflare 403); the hours and ID pages were read through Chrome. Registration and selfie sources are county election offices, not the state: the Oct. 5 date is from Liberty County's reproduction of the SOS '2026 State Election Comprehensive Calendar' (row: election date, advance voting window, registration deadline); the selfie quote is O.C.G.A. 21-2-413(e) as quoted in Chatham County Elections' media policy, because the official Georgia Code (LexisNexis) could not be fetched. The 21-2-413(e) text also lets a poll manager allow photography and, per search summaries, bars photographing a ballot being voted; I did not read that clause directly. Upgrade both sources to sos.ga.gov if possible.

polls.summary: Hawaii votes by mail. Your ballot must be received by 7 p.m. on November 3. Voter service centers are open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. that day for in-person voting.
polls.quote: General Election October 20, 2026, through November 2, 2026 Monday through Saturday 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. November 3, 2026 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.

id.summary: Most voters don't need to show ID. At a voter service center, you may confirm who you are with your license or Social Security digits, or show ID if asked.
id.quote: A clerk may choose to verify a voter's identity, without the above application. As such, the voter may be asked for one of the following: (1) The provision of a current and valid photo identification

registration.deadline: Monday, October 26, 2026 at 4:30 p.m. for paper applications (10th day before the election). After that, same-day registration at voter service centers from October 20 through Election Day.
registration.summary: Paper registration forms were due October 26, 2026. You can also register and vote the same day at a voter service center, open October 20 through November 3.
registration.quote: If you miss the registration deadline, same day voter registration is available at voter service centers, to register and vote in-person, beginning 10 days prior and through election day.

HI.notes: Ballots arrive by mail about 18 days before the election and must be received (not postmarked) by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. The Office of Elections page also says 'Voters may register online at any time or in-person at a voter service center,' which does not state an online cutoff; only the paper deadline is confirmed. ID rule is from Hawaii Administrative Rules ch. 3-177 (Office of Elections PDF): identity is verified mainly through an application using a driver license, state ID, or SSN4, or the clerk may ask for photo ID, a utility bill, oral recitation of record details, or a vouching witness; quote's OCR typos ('piovision') were corrected to 'provision'. First-time mail registrants without HAVA ID vote provisionally. capitol.hawaii.gov (HRS) blocked fetching, so no statute on ballot photos could be checked; selfie is null.

polls.summary: Polls are open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. local time. Some counties open at 7 a.m. Idaho has two time zones. If you are in line at 8 p.m., you can vote.
polls.quote: the polls shall be opened at 8:00 A.M. and remain open until all registered electors of that precinct have appeared and voted or until 8:00 P.M. of the same day, whichever comes first.

id.summary: You'll be asked for a photo ID, such as an Idaho driver's license, U.S. passport, or tribal ID. If you don't have one, you can sign an identity affidavit.
id.quote: A registered voter may sign a Personal Identification Affidavit instead of presenting photo identification.

registration.deadline: Friday, October 23, 2026 (registrations must reach the county clerk by 5 p.m. local time; online deadline is 11 days before the election). After that, register in person at early voting or at your polling place on Election Day with photo ID and proof of residence.
registration.summary: Pre-registration closed October 23, 2026. You can still register and vote in person during early voting or on Election Day if you bring a photo ID and proof of residence.
registration.quote: The deadline to register to vote online is 11 days before an election. You may also register when you vote in person at early voting or on Election Day.

ID.notes: Oct. 23 date and 5 p.m. local time are from the VoteIdaho calendar event 'Preregistration Deadline' (voteidaho.gov/event/preregistration-deadline-2/), citing Idaho Code 34-408 and 34-410. Idaho has two time zones (Mountain and, in the northern panhandle, Pacific); the 'local time' wording is mine, based on the statute's reference to county clerks. ID list also includes a concealed weapons license; Idaho does not use provisional ballots (VoteIdaho FAQ). Selfie: no provision found in Idaho Code Title 34 ch. 11 or Title 18 ch. 23 section titles, and no VoteIdaho guidance.

polls.summary: Polls are open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m.
polls.quote: Sec. 17-1. The polls shall be opened at the hour of 6:00 a.m. and continued open until 7:00 p.m. of the same day, at which time the polls shall be closed

id.summary: Most voters just give their name and sign in. If you first registered by mail and haven't proven your identity, you must vote in person and may need ID.
id.quote: Any person desiring to vote shall give his name and, if required to do so, his residence to the judges of election

registration.deadline: Tuesday, October 6, 2026 for regular in-person and mail registration (mail must be postmarked before registration closes); online registration through Sunday, October 18, 2026 (16 days before). Grace period registration and voting in person at designated sites from October 7 through Election Day.
registration.summary: Regular registration closed October 6, and online registration runs through October 18, 2026. After that, you can register and vote in person through Election Day at designated grace period sites.
registration.quote: Regular registration is open all year except the 27 day period prior to Election Day. Online registration is open until 16 days before Election Day. Grace period registration and voting begins the 27th day prior to Election Day

IL.notes: Dates are computed from the State Board's rules (closes 28 days before = Oct. 6; online until 16 days before = Oct. 18); no 2026 calendar page with the dates was fetched (the SBE calendar page returned almost no content). Grace period voting details: elections.il.gov grace period document (10 ILCS 5/4-50, 5-50, 6-100). Selfie: 10 ILCS 5/29-9 makes it a Class 4 felony to knowingly mark a ballot 'so that it can be observed by another person'; it does not mention photographs, and no State Board guidance on ballot photos was found, so this is left null rather than inferred. The first-time mail registrant ID rule is from the SBE 'Registering to Vote in Illinois' document.

polls.summary: Polls are open 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. local time. Indiana has two time zones, so check which one your county uses.
polls.quote: The polls must remain open continuously from 6:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. prevailing local time.

id.summary: You must show a current photo ID from Indiana or the U.S. government, such as a driver's license or U.S. passport. Without one, you vote provisionally and must follow up.
id.quote: If you cast a provisional ballot, you have until noon 10 days after the election to follow up with the county election board and either provide the necessary documentation or affirm one of the law’s exemptions applies to you.

registration.deadline: Monday, October 5, 2026 for online, mail (postmarked), and in-person registration.
registration.summary: The deadline to register for the November 3 election was October 5, 2026. Indiana does not offer same-day or Election Day registration.
registration.quote: On or before April 6, 2026 before the 2026 Primary Election, or on or before October 5, 2026 before the 2026 General Election.

IN.notes: Changed recently: effective July 1, 2025, college and university IDs no longer count as voter ID (SOS Photo ID Law page). ID must show name, photo, and an expiration date that is current or after the last general election. The Oct. 5 quote is on the SOS registration page under mail and in-person registration; the page does not give a separate online date, so 'online' in the deadline is an assumption to recheck. Selfie: the 2026 Election Day Handbook lets voters use cell phones in the polls if they don't electioneer or disrupt, but says nothing about ballot photos. Indiana's 2015 ballot-selfie ban (IC 3-11-8-17.5) was blocked by a federal court; no current official guidance was found, so this is null.

polls.summary: Polls are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.
polls.quote: the polls shall be opened at 7:00 a.m. if at least one official from each of the political parties referred to in section 49.13 is present ... The polling places shall be closed at 8:00 p.m. for all elections.

id.summary: You must show ID, such as an Iowa driver's license, U.S. passport, or the free Iowa Voter ID Card. Without it, another registered voter can attest for you.
id.quote: Iowa voters are required to show an Iowa driver’s license or non-operator ID, U.S. passport, U.S. military ID or veteran’s ID, tribal ID/document, or Iowa voter ID card at the polls before they vote.

registration.deadline: Monday, October 19, 2026 (pre-registration closes 15 days before the election). After that, register at your polling place on Election Day with proof of identity and residence.
registration.summary: Pre-registration closes October 19, 2026. After that, you can register and vote at your correct polling place on Election Day if you bring ID and proof of where you live.
registration.quote: You may register and vote on election day. To do so, you first must go to the correct polling place for your current address on election day.

selfie.summary: Iowa law bans photos and showing your voted ballot only if done for an illegal purpose, or if it interferes with other voters or the polling place.
selfie.quote: The use of photographic devices and the display of voted ballots is prohibited if such use or display is for purposes prohibited under chapter 39A, interferes with other voters, or interferes with the orderly operation of the polling place.

IA.notes: The Oct. 19 date is computed from the SOS rule 'Pre-Registration Deadlines 15 days before the election' (Nov. 3 minus 15 days); no 2026 calendar was checked. The Iowa Voter ID Card has no photo, which is why this is id_nonphoto; Iowa Code chapter 49 lists the accepted IDs; tribal IDs need a photo, signature, and expiration date. Iowa Code 49.73 lets some polling places open later than 7 a.m. for some elections based on turnout; the 7 a.m. opening is the default. Selfie rule is a judgment call: Iowa Code 49.88(1) does not ban ballot photos outright, only for prohibited purposes or when disruptive. The Election Day FAQ says the media may not photograph how a voter marks a ballot.

polls.summary: Polls are open at least 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Counties may open as early as 6 a.m. and close as late as 8 p.m., so check your county's hours.
polls.quote: State law requires polling places to open at 7:00 a.m. and close at 7:00 p.m. on election day. State law allow counties to open polling locations as early as 6:00 a.m. and close as late as 8:00 p.m.

id.summary: You must show a photo ID, such as a driver's license, U.S. passport, or Kansas college student ID. Without one, you vote a provisional ballot.
id.quote: State law requires Kansas voters to show photographic identification when casting a vote in person, this includes voting advance in-person. If the voter does not provide identification or it is not valid, the voter will be issued a provisional ballot.

registration.deadline: Tuesday, October 13, 2026 (registration closes 21 days before the election; mailed applications must be postmarked by then).
registration.summary: The deadline to register for the November 3 election was October 13, 2026. Kansas does not offer same-day or Election Day registration.
registration.quote: you have to be registered 21 days prior to an election and be a resident of Kansas at the time of registration.

KS.notes: The Oct. 13 date is computed from the 21-day rule (Nov. 3 minus 21 days); the SOS registration form also says 'Voter registration closes 21 days before any election.' Kansas spans Central and Mountain time zones; the SOS page doesn't say 'local time.' Voters 65 and older may use an expired photo ID; religious-objection exemption via Form DRO. New Kansas residents who miss the deadline can vote a president-only ballot in presidential years only, so it doesn't apply in 2026. Selfie: no statute or SOS guidance on ballot photos found in the SOS FAQ or Election Standards Chapter II.

polls.summary: Polls are open 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. local time. Kentucky has two time zones. If you are in line by 6 p.m., you can vote.
polls.quote: In-person voting on Election Day, November 3, 2026, will take place from 6:00AM to 6:00PM, local time.

id.summary: You'll be asked for a photo ID, such as a Kentucky driver's license, U.S. passport, or military ID. If you can't get one, you can sign an affirmation and vote.
id.quote: if a voter is unable to provide proof of identification as required under KRS 117.225, and as defined under KRS 117.001, a voter may cast a ballot if the individual ... executes a voter's affirmation (2) In addition to the requirements of subsection (1) of this section, to cast a ballot, the voter who is unable to provide proof of identification shall provide to an election officer: (a) Any identification card issued by a county in this state ... or (b) Any identification card with the voter's photograph and the name of the voter stated.

registration.deadline: Monday, October 5, 2026: online by 4 p.m. local time, mail postmarked by October 5, or in person at the county clerk's office by close of business.
registration.summary: The deadline to register for the November 3 election was October 5, 2026. Kentucky does not offer same-day or Election Day registration; the rolls freeze after the deadline.
registration.quote: Last Day to register to vote Monday October 5, 2026: Register Online by 4pm local time. Mailed Registration Cards can be Postmarked on 10/5 to be accepted.

KY.notes: ID: the affirmation route (KRS 117.228) requires the voter to state one of a list of 'reasonable impediments' to getting photo ID and, per news and advocacy summaries, to show a non-photo ID; the second part was not confirmed in the official text, which was truncated in my extract. Accepted photo IDs are listed on the State Board's Voter ID Requirements page (elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Absentee-Excused-In-Person.aspx). Registration FAQ says 'once the voter registration deadline has passed, the voter registration rolls are frozen until after the next election.' Selfie: KRS 117.235 (voting room rules) was read and 117.236 checked by title; neither addresses ballot photos, and no State Board guidance was found.

polls.summary: On Tuesday, November 3, polls are open 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. If you are in line at 8 p.m., you can vote.
polls.quote: On election day, the polls are open from 6 a.m.-8 p.m.

id.summary: You'll be asked for a photo ID with your signature, such as a Louisiana driver's license or special ID card. Without one, you can sign a voter affidavit and vote.
id.quote: Be prepared to show a photo identification card with your photo and signature or a United States military identification card that contains your name and picture when voting.

registration.deadline: Monday, October 5, 2026 in person, by mail (postmarked), or at an OMV office; Tuesday, October 13, 2026 through the GeauxVote Online Registration System.
registration.summary: The deadline to register in person or by mail was October 5, and online was October 13, 2026. Louisiana does not offer same-day or Election Day registration.
registration.quote: The deadline to register to vote in person, by mail, or at an OMV Office is October 5. The deadline to register to vote through the GeauxVote Online Registration System is October 13.

LA.notes: Nov. 3, 2026 in Louisiana is the U.S. Senate general and the open primary for several offices; a December 12, 2026 election follows for some races. Polls open at 6 a.m. for Tuesday elections and 7 a.m. for Saturday elections. The ID quote omits a middle clause about getting a free special ID card at the OMV. Selfie: NCSL cites La. R.S. 18:1461.7 (a voter may not allow a ballot to be seen) and news reports cite R.S. 18:1461.3 on recording devices, with conflicting SOS statements over the years; I could not open either section on legis.la.gov or find current SOS guidance, so this is null.

polls.open: 6 a.m. to 10 a.m., set by each town
polls.summary: Polls close at 8 p.m. Opening time is set by each town, between 6 a.m. and 8 a.m. (as late as 10 a.m. in towns under 500 people). Check your town's hours.
polls.quote: The polls must be opened no earlier than 6 a.m. and no later than 8 a.m. on election day, except that in municipalities with a population of less than 500, the polls must be opened no later than 10:00 a.m.

id.summary: Registered voters don't need to show ID. You state your name and address to the election clerk. If you register in person, you must show proof of identity and residency.
id.quote: A voter who wishes to vote must state the voter's name and residence address to an election clerk, who shall announce the name in a loud, clear voice.

registration.deadline: Tuesday, October 13, 2026 (21st day before the election): by mail or third party by close of business, online by 5 p.m. In person, you can register until the polls close on Election Day.
registration.summary: Mail and online registration closed October 13, 2026. You can still register in person with your town's registrar through Election Day, including at the polls.
registration.quote: D. If submitted in person, the close of the polls on election day.

selfie.summary: Anyone taking photos in the voting place must stay outside the voting area and 15 feet from voters, but you may photograph only yourself. Ballot photos aren't addressed.
selfie.quote: A person video recording or engaging in still photography in the voting place ... must remain outside the guardrail enclosure ... except that a person may take a still photograph that depicts only the person taking the photograph.

ME.notes: Changed recently: PL 2025, c. 397 rewrote the registration deadline (21-A §121-A) and added the photography rule (§683(5)). maine.gov/sos returned 403 to every fetch, so all answers rest on the Maine Revised Statutes (legislature.maine.gov). The Oct. 13 date is computed from the 21-day rule. Maine voters considered a photo ID citizen initiative in November 2025; the current §671 still has voters state name and address only, but I did not confirm the initiative's outcome on an official page. Selfie classification is a judgment call: §683(5) addresses where photography can happen and allows self-photos but does not mention photographing or sharing a marked ballot; no statute banning ballot display was found in §§671 to 683.

polls.summary: Polls are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. on November 3. Mail-in ballots must be postmarked or put in a drop box by 8 p.m.
polls.quote: Vote on Election Day Election day polling places will be open from 7:00 am until 8:00 pm

id.summary: Most voters don't show ID. Some first-time voters will be asked for ID, such as a Maryland driver's license, student ID, or a utility bill.
id.quote: Some first time voters in Maryland will be asked to show ID before voting.

registration.deadline: Tuesday, October 13, 2026 (online by 11:59 p.m., or by application). After that, register in person during early voting (October 22 to 29) or at your assigned polling place on Election Day with proof of residence.
registration.summary: The advance deadline was October 13, 2026. You can still register and vote during early voting or at your polling place on Election Day if you bring a document showing where you live.
registration.quote: You can also register to vote during early voting or on election day. Go to an early voting center in the county where you live during early voting , or go to your assigned election day polling place

selfie.summary: You may photograph your own marked ballot before casting it, for personal use. Otherwise, phones and cameras can't be used in polling places except for a few reasons.
selfie.quote: You cannot use your cell phone, pager, camera, and computer equipment in an early voting center or at a polling place except to ... record a digital image of your marked ballot prior to casting for personal use.

MD.notes: Deadline quote: 'For the 2026 Gubernatorial General Election, the advanced deadline to register to vote and update your information is Tuesday, October 13, 2026' (Election Day Questions page). Selfie: the State Board allows a photo of your own marked ballot 'for personal use'; it doesn't say whether posting it publicly counts, so a stricter reader might call this 'limited.' The underlying rule is in COMAR/Election Law, not checked directly.

polls.open: 7 a.m. (some towns as early as 5:45 a.m.)
polls.summary: Polls close at 8 p.m. They open by 7 a.m., and some cities and towns open as early as 5:45 a.m. Check your town's hours.
polls.quote: At state elections the polls shall not be closed before eight o'clock in the evening. In cities and towns at the election of state officers, the polls may be open as early as fifteen minutes before six o'clock

id.summary: Most voters don't need ID. Some first-time voters who registered by mail must show a photo ID or a document like a utility bill. Poll workers may also ask.
id.quote: a person desiring to vote, who fails to present suitable written identification when so requested by an election officer, shall be permitted to vote, but that person's right to vote may be challenged under section 85.

registration.deadline: Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 5 p.m. (10th day before the election). Mailed forms postmarked by midnight that day count.
registration.summary: The deadline to register is October 24, 2026, at 5 p.m., or by mail postmarked that day. Massachusetts does not offer same-day or Election Day registration.
registration.quote: registration for the next election shall take place no later than 5:00 p.m. on the tenth day preceding such election

selfie.summary: State law makes it a crime to let anyone see how you marked your ballot for any purpose not allowed by law, which covers sharing a photo of it.
selfie.quote: Whoever, at a primary, caucus or election, ... allows the marking of his ballot to be seen by any person for any purpose not authorized by law ... shall be punished

MA.notes: sec.state.ma.us pages fetched once and then returned an Incapsula block, so all answers rest on the General Laws at malegislature.gov. The Oct. 24 date is computed from the 10-day rule (Nov. 3 minus 10 = Saturday, Oct. 24); I did not confirm the Secretary's published date. Same-day registration: none found in c. 51 §26 (exceptions in §§34 and 50 are not Election Day registration). Selfie: c. 56 §25 does not mention photos; 'not_allowed' is an inference from the ban on letting your marked ballot be seen. The Secretary of the Commonwealth has said publicly in past years that ballot selfies are illegal, but I did not find that on an official page this session.

polls.summary: Polls are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. local time. If you are in line at 8 p.m., you can still vote.
polls.quote: Voters can visit their assigned polling place on Election Day from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. local time.

id.summary: If you have a photo ID, such as a driver's license, U.S. passport, or student ID, you must show it. If you don't, you can sign an affidavit and vote.
id.quote: Voters are not required to possess a photo ID to vote in Michigan. Voters without a photo ID may sign an affidavit and will be issued a ballot.

registration.deadline: Monday, October 19, 2026 (15 days before) for online and mail (postmarked) registration. From October 20 through 8 p.m. on Election Day, register in person at your local clerk's office with proof of residency.
registration.summary: Online and mail registration closes October 19, 2026. After that, you can register in person at your city or township clerk's office through 8 p.m. on Election Day and vote.
registration.quote: Within 14 days of an election, voters must submit a voter registration application in person and present proof of residency at their local clerk’s office.

selfie.summary: You may photograph your own ballot in the voting booth, but you can't hold it up for a selfie. Take selfies outside the polling place.
selfie.quote: Voters can take a picture of their own ballot in the voting booth. For the privacy and security of neighboring voters, voters are prohibited from holding their ballot up for a selfie and/or photo.

MI.notes: CONTRADICTION: the SOS 'Vote on Election Day' page lists 'Do take a selfie outside the voting area' and 'Do not take a photo within the voting area,' while the SOS Elections FAQ says voters can photograph their own ballot in the voting booth. 'Limited' tries to cover both; recheck before publishing. The Oct. 19 date is computed from the 15-day rule (Nov. 3 minus 15). Same-day registrants vote at the clerk's office (absentee ballot) or take the receipt to their polling place or an Election Day Vote Center.

polls.summary: Polls are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Some small towns open later, but no later than 10 a.m. Check your town's hours.
polls.quote: at the state primary and the state general election the hours for voting in every precinct in the state shall begin at 7:00 a.m. and shall extend continuously until 8:00 p.m.

id.summary: If you are already registered, you don't need to show ID. You sign the polling place roster. If you register at the polls, you need proof of residence.
id.quote: An individual seeking to vote shall sign a polling place roster or voter signature certificate which states that the individual: (1) is at least 18 years old

registration.deadline: Tuesday, October 13, 2026 (registration closes during the 20 days before the election). After that, register at your polling place on Election Day with proof of residence.
registration.summary: Pre-registration closed October 13, 2026. You can still register at your polling place on Election Day if you bring proof of where you live.
registration.quote: At any time except during the 20 days immediately preceding any regularly scheduled election, an eligible voter ... may register or update a registration to vote

selfie.summary: In the polling place, you may not reveal your vote or show your marked ballot to anyone. If you do, election judges set your ballot aside as spoiled.
selfie.quote: If a voter, after marking a ballot, shows it to anyone except as authorized by law, the election judges shall refuse to deposit the ballot in any ballot box and shall place it among the spoiled ballots.

MN.notes: sos.mn.gov blocked all fetches (CAPTCHA), so answers rest on Minnesota Statutes at revisor.mn.gov. The Oct. 13 date is computed (last day before the 20-day closed period). The revisor flags that 201.061 subd. 3 (Election Day registration proof) was amended in the 2026 session; check effective dates. Selfie: 204C.17 does not mention photos; 'limited' reflects that it bars showing a marked ballot or revealing your vote inside the polling place, and says nothing about mail ballots. The SOS has said in past years that ballot photos aren't allowed at the polls; not confirmed on an official page this session.

polls.summary: Polls are open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. on November 3.
polls.quote: 3rd General Election Day and Regular Special Election Day. Polls open from 7 a.m. - 7 p.m.

id.summary: You must show a photo ID, such as a Mississippi driver's license or U.S. passport. Without one, you vote by affidavit and have five business days to show ID.
id.quote: A voter who does not have photo ID on Election Day will be asked to vote by affidavit ballot at the polling place. The voter will then have five (5) business days to show an acceptable form of photo ID

registration.deadline: Monday, October 5, 2026, in person at the Circuit Clerk's or Municipal Clerk's office, or by mail postmarked by that day.
registration.summary: The deadline to register for the November 3 election was October 5, 2026, in person or by mail. Mississippi does not offer same-day or Election Day registration.
registration.quote: 5th Voter Registration Deadline (General): Applicants who register in-person in the Circuit Clerk’s office or Municipal Clerk’s office today, and those who mail registration applications post-marked no later than today are eligible to vote in the General Election.

MS.notes: Calendar is the SOS 2026 Elections Calendar (last revised 9/8/2026). The calendar lists only in-person and mail registration for this deadline; I did not see an online option. A runoff, if needed, is Dec. 1, 2026, with a Nov. 2 registration deadline. msvoterid.ms.gov is the Secretary of State's voter ID site. Selfie: no statute or SOS guidance on voters photographing ballots found; the 2026 County Election Handbook only cites an AG opinion that ballots should not be photographed during a ballot box examination.

polls.summary: Polls are open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. If you are in line at 7 p.m., you can still vote.
polls.quote: POLLING PLACES ARE OPEN FROM 6:00 AM TO 7:00 PM ON ELECTION DAY. Important: If you are in line at the closing time of 7:00 PM you have the right to cast your vote

id.summary: You must show a photo ID, such as a Missouri driver's license or U.S. passport. Without one, you vote provisionally; it counts if you bring ID or your signature matches.
id.quote: If you do not possess any of these forms of identification, but are a registered voter, you may cast a provisional ballot.

registration.deadline: Wednesday, October 7, 2026 (4th Wednesday before the election); mailed forms must be postmarked by then. Online registration is also available.
registration.summary: The deadline to register for the November 3 election was October 7, 2026. Missouri does not offer same-day or Election Day registration.
registration.quote: November 3, 2026 General Election October 7, 2026

selfie.summary: State law makes it an election offense to let anyone see your ballot to show how you voted, which would cover sharing a photo of it.
selfie.quote: allowing his or her ballot to be seen by any person with the intent of letting it be known how he or she is about to vote or has voted

MO.notes: Changed recently: Missouri's photo ID requirement took effect in 2022 (HB 1878); the SOS page reflects it, including that a provisional ballot counts if you return with photo ID on Election Day or your signature matches. The calendar quote is from a table whose columns are 'Official Election Day, Style of Election, Last Day to Register to Vote...'; the SOS register page says forms must be 'POSTMARKED by the 4th Wednesday before the election.' Selfie: RSMo 115.637(14) does not mention photos; 'not_allowed' is an inference from the intent-based ban on letting your ballot be seen. No SOS guidance on ballot selfies found.

polls.close: 8 p.m. (drop box and in-person return deadline)
polls.summary: Oregon votes by mail. Return your ballot to a drop box or county elections office by 8 p.m. on Election Day, or mail it postmarked by Election Day; it counts if it arrives within 7 days. County offices are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Election Day.
polls.quote: Ballots that are mailed must be postmarked by Election Day. Ballots that are postmarked by Election Day can be received by local elections offices up to 7 days after Election Day and be counted.

id.summary: Oregon votes by mail, and you do not show ID to vote. Your county checks the signature on your ballot return envelope against your voter registration record.
id.quote: Your county elections office compares the signature on the ballot return identification envelope to the signatures in the voter’s registration record.

registration.deadline: Tuesday, October 13, 2026 (21 days before Election Day). Online registration must be submitted by 11:59:59 p.m. Pacific Time that day.
registration.summary: Register by October 13, 2026, online, by mail, or in person at your county elections office. Oregon has no Election Day registration.
registration.quote: Voter registration deadline : October 13

OR.notes: County office hours quote: 'County elections offices are open 7 am - 8 pm on Election Day.' Oregon spans two time zones (most of Malheur County is Mountain); deadline is 8 p.m. local per county office. ID: first-time registrants who did not give a DMV or SSN number may be asked for ID with the ballot (HAVA); not verified on an Oregon page. Selfie: news reports quote the SOS saying a ban on showing a marked ballot was repealed in 2014 and selfies are legal, but no official SOS page or ORS text confirming it was found.

polls.summary: Polls are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Election Day, November 3, 2026.
polls.quote: Polls are open on election day from 7 A.M. - 8 P.M.

id.summary: Most voters do not show ID. If it is your first time voting at your polling place, bring photo or non-photo ID, such as a driver's license or utility bill.
id.quote: No . Unless it's your first time voting at a new polling place. If it's your first time voting at a new location, you must bring one of the approved forms of identification .

registration.deadline: Monday, October 19, 2026 (online, by mail, or in person).
registration.summary: The last day to register for the November 3 election is October 19, 2026. Pennsylvania has no Election Day registration.
registration.quote: Last day to register to vote : Oct. 19, 2026

PA.notes: Accepted first-time IDs include a PA driver's license or PennDOT ID, student ID, current utility bill, bank statement, or paycheck (pa.gov new-voters page). Selfie: no Department of State FAQ or rules-at-the-polls text addresses ballot photos; Election Code text was not checked on an official site. Leave null unless verified.

polls.summary: Polls are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Election Day. In New Shoreham (Block Island), polls open at 9 a.m.
polls.quote: The polls will be open on Election Day from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. (except in New Shoreham, where polls open at 9 a.m.).

id.summary: Bring a photo ID, such as a RI driver's license, free RI voter ID card, or U.S. passport. Without one, your provisional ballot counts if your signature matches.
id.quote: The local board shall examine each provisional ballot application to determine if the signature matches the signature on the voter’s registration. If the local board determines that the signatures match, the provisional ballot shall count.

registration.deadline: Registration closes on the 30th day before the election, which is Sunday, October 4, 2026.
registration.summary: Registration closes 30 days before the election, on October 4, 2026. You cannot register on Election Day for this election.
registration.quote: Registration for any election shall close on the thirtieth (30th) day preceding an election

RI.notes: vote.ri.gov / vote.sos.ri.gov HTML pages block curl; the 2026 Voter Information Handbook PDF and RI General Laws were used. ID statute 17-19-24.2 lists photo IDs; a voter without one votes provisionally under 17-19-24.3 (signature match). The Oct 4 date falls on a Sunday; statute says local boards don't take registrations Sundays, so in-person may effectively end Friday Oct 2 while online may run through Oct 4; not confirmed on an official 2026 page. RI allows an emergency presidential-only ballot for late registrants in presidential years (general knowledge, not verified); not relevant in 2026. Selfie: nothing found in chapters 17-19 or 17-23.

polls.summary: Polling places are open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Election Day. Anyone in line at 7 p.m. can vote.
polls.quote: Polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. Anyone in line at 7:00 p.m. will be allowed to vote.

id.summary: You will be asked for a photo ID, such as a SC driver's license or U.S. passport. If you cannot get one, show your voter card and sign an impediment affidavit.
id.quote: If you cannot get a photo ID , bring your non-photo voter registration card with you to the polling place.

registration.deadline: Online by Sunday, October 4, 2026; fax or email received by October 4; mail postmarked by Monday, October 5; in person at most county offices by 5 p.m. Friday, October 2.
registration.summary: Register online by October 4, by mail postmarked by October 5, or in person by October 2 at most county offices. South Carolina has no same-day registration.
registration.quote: Register online at scVOTES.gov (must be received by Sunday, October 4 ).

selfie.summary: State law makes it unlawful for a voter to let anyone see their ballot. State law enforcement has warned this includes taking or sharing ballot photos.
selfie.quote: It is unlawful in any election for a voter to: (1) allow his ballot to be seen by a person, except as provided by law

SC.notes: ID: if you forget a photo ID you have, you vote provisionally and must show it to the county office before certification; the reasonable impediment affidavit route is for voters who could not obtain one. The selfie classification relies on SC Code 7-25-100 plus a 2024 SLED warning reported by news outlets (SLED's own release not opened). Polls quote also appears on the 2026prep page. Registration quote applies to the Nov 3, 2026 general (2026prep page).
