polls.summary: Polls are open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time. South Dakota spans the Central and Mountain time zones.
polls.quote: Polls are open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time.

id.summary: You will be asked for a photo ID, such as a South Dakota driver's license. Without one, you can sign a personal identification affidavit and vote a regular ballot.
id.quote: If you do not have a photo ID, you can sign a personal identification affidavit, and will still be allowed to vote a regular ballot.

registration.deadline: Your signed form must be received by your county auditor by Monday, October 19, 2026 (15 days before the election).
registration.summary: Your registration form must reach your county auditor by October 19, 2026. South Dakota has no Election Day registration.
registration.quote: Your Voter Registration form with an original signature must be received by the auditor 15 days before any election if you wish to vote in that election.

selfie.summary: State law says no one may publicize a marked ballot in a way that reveals the votes on it, which would include sharing a ballot photo.
selfie.quote: No person may publicize an official ballot after it is marked to any person in such a way as to reveal the contents of the official ballot

SD.notes: Oct 19 computed from the 15-day rule. Statute was read through the legislature API (https://sdlegislature.gov/api/Statutes/12-18-27.html); the public page URL is given as source. Selfie classification is a reading of 12-18-27; no SOS FAQ on selfies found. Check whether 2026 legislation changed the ID affidavit; the sdsos page as fetched still describes it.

polls.summary: Opening times vary by county. All polls close at 8 p.m. Eastern or 7 p.m. Central time. If you are in line at closing, you can vote. Check GoVoteTN for your polling place hours.
polls.quote: On Election Day, poll opening times vary by county. Voters should check their polling location and hours before heading to the polls. All polls close at 8 p.m. EDT / 7 p.m. CDT.

id.summary: You must show a federal or Tennessee photo ID, such as a Tennessee driver's license, U.S. passport, or military ID. Expired IDs work. College IDs do not.
id.quote: All voters must present a federal or Tennessee state ID containing the voter’s name and photograph when voting at the polls, whether voting early or on Election Day unless an exemption below applies.

registration.deadline: 11:59 p.m. Monday, October 5, 2026 (online; mail forms postmarked 30 days before).
registration.summary: Registration for the November 3 election closed at 11:59 p.m. on October 5, 2026. Tennessee has no Election Day registration.
registration.quote: Eligible citizens must submit their voter registration application by 11:59 p.m. on Monday, Oct. 5, 2026, to be eligible to vote in the upcoming election.

selfie.summary: You may use your phone in the polling place for information, but state law bars taking photos or videos there, so no ballot selfies at the polls.
selfie.quote: Tennessee Code Annotated § 2-7-142 permits voters to use mobile electronic devices inside polling places to assist in making election decisions, but prohibits use of the devices for telephone conversations, photography, and video or audio recordings.

TN.notes: Poll-hours quote comes from the Aug 6, 2026 election press release; same rule expected Nov 3. Without photo ID you vote provisionally and have two business days to show ID at the election commission (sos.tn.gov FAQ). Selfie source is a 2016 AG opinion describing T.C.A. 2-7-142; a 2017 Senate bill to allow ballot photos passed the Senate, and its final status was not confirmed, so check current 2-7-142 text. Mail/absentee ballot photos are not addressed.

polls.summary: Polls are open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time on Election Day. Texas spans the Central and Mountain time zones.
polls.quote: The hours of voting on election day are 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.

id.summary: Show one of seven photo IDs, such as a Texas driver's license or U.S. passport. If you cannot reasonably get one, sign a Reasonable Impediment Declaration and show supporting ID.
id.quote: you can use your valid voter registration certificate as a form of supporting identification when you execute your Reasonable Impediment Declaration, and vote a regular ballot.

registration.deadline: Monday, October 5, 2026 (postmark date or in-person delivery to your county voter registrar).
registration.summary: The registration deadline for the November 3 election was October 5, 2026. Texas has no same-day or Election Day registration.
registration.quote: The voter registration deadline for the November 3, 2026 Uniform Election is October 5, 2026.

selfie.summary: You may not use a phone where voting happens or record images within 100 feet of a voting station, so no ballot selfies at the polls.
selfie.quote: A person may not use any mechanical or electronic means of recording images or sound within 100 feet of a voting station.

TX.notes: Statute page read in Chrome (Texas Election Code 61.014). Supporting-ID alternatives for the Reasonable Impediment Declaration also include a utility bill, bank statement, or birth certificate (not quoted). Texas does not offer full online registration (general knowledge, not verified).

polls.summary: Utah mails ballots to voters. Your mail ballot must be received by the clerk by 8 p.m. on Election Day, November 3, 2026; a postmark is not enough. You can also use a drop box or vote in person, 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.
polls.quote: Your mail ballot must received by the clerk’s office on or before 8:00 p.m. on Election Day, November 3, 2026. Ballots received after November 3, 2026 will not be counted.

id.summary: To vote in person, show one photo ID, such as a Utah driver's license or U.S. passport, or two documents that together prove your name and address.
id.quote: TWO forms of ID that, when combined, prove your name and current residence.

registration.deadline: Your county clerk must receive your registration by 5 p.m. Friday, October 23, 2026. After that, you can register in person at an early voting location or on Election Day with two forms of ID.
registration.summary: Register by 5 p.m. October 23, 2026. After that, you can still register in person during early voting or on Election Day with two forms of ID.
registration.quote: Registration must be received by the county clerk by the deadline above. Voters may register in-person on Election Day with two forms of valid ID.

selfie.summary: State law lets you photograph your own ballot and share the photo. Photographing someone else's ballot at a polling place is a misdemeanor.
selfie.quote: Subsection (1) does not prohibit an individual from transferring a photograph of the individual's own ballot in a manner that allows the photograph to be viewed by the individual or another.

UT.notes: Changed recently: Utah used to count mail ballots postmarked before Election Day; a 2025 law (HB 300, per general knowledge) changed this, and the 2026 vote.utah.gov page confirms ballots must be received by 8 p.m. In-person poll hours are from Utah Code 20A-1-302 ('Polls at all elections on the date of the election shall open at 7 a.m. and shall remain open until 8 p.m.'). Same-day registrants vote a provisional ballot. The ID page also accepts a tribal ID without a photo.

polls.open: Between 5 a.m. and 10 a.m. (set by each town)
polls.summary: Vermont mails a general election ballot to every active voter. Return it to your town clerk before the office closes the day before the election, or to your polling place by 7 p.m. on Election Day. Polls open between 5 and 10 a.m., depending on the town.
polls.quote: Return your ballot to your town clerk’s office before the office closes on the day before the election, or bring it to your polling place before 7 p.m. on Election Day.

id.summary: Most voters do not show ID. First-time registrants who register by mail or online must send a copy of an ID, such as a driver's license or utility bill.
id.quote: If you are registering to vote in Vermont for the first time by mail or online, you must include a photocopy of an acceptable form of ID.

registration.deadline: No advance deadline. You can register during your town or city clerk's business hours before the election or at the polls during voting hours on Election Day, November 3, 2026.
registration.summary: You can register at your town clerk's office any business day before the election, or at your polling place on Election Day.
registration.quote: Registration is available during all normal business hours of your town or city clerk's office on days preceding the election and during polling hours on Election Day. 17 V.S.A. § 2144

VT.notes: Poll opening hours quote: 'All polls in Vermont open between 5 and 10 a.m. and close at 7 p.m.' (sos.vermont.gov voters page). All-mail quote: 'Vermont automatically mails general election ballots to all qualified voters by October 1 of each even-numbered year.' Mail ballots are not counted by postmark; they must arrive by close of polls. ID: whether a first-time mail registrant who sent no ID must show one at the polls is not stated on the page fetched (HAVA rule). Selfie: no provision found in 17 V.S.A. chapters 35, 49, or 51 (only a rule that justice-assisted absentee voters mark ballots without exhibiting them); no SOS guidance found.

polls.summary: Polling places are open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Election Day. Anyone in line at 7 p.m. can vote.
polls.quote: Polling places are open from 6:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. Anyone in line at 7:00 p.m. will be allowed to vote.

id.summary: Show an acceptable ID, which does not need a photo. If you do not have one, you can sign an ID Confirmation Statement and vote a regular ballot.
id.quote: Virginia law requires all voters to provide either an acceptable form of ID or sign an ID Confirmation Statement at the polls.

registration.deadline: Register or update by Friday, October 23, 2026. After that, you can register in person and vote a provisional ballot through Election Day.
registration.summary: Register by October 23, 2026. After that, you can still register in person and vote a provisional ballot during early voting or at your polling place on Election Day.
registration.quote: Voters may register and vote using a provisional ballot In-Person after October 23, 2026, through Election Day.

selfie.summary: You may generally use phones and other electronic devices inside the polling place. Election officers can stop use that disrupts voting or tries to influence other voters.
selfie.quote: The use of electronic devices inside the polling place is generally permitted.

VA.notes: Registration deadline for Nov 3, 2026 is listed as 10/23/2026 on ELECT's upcoming-elections page, later than the 22-day rule some older pages show (the same-day registration FAQ still mentions an 'October 24' deadline from a past year). Verify before publishing. Accepted IDs include non-photo documents like a utility bill or voter card (ELECT list not opened). Selfie: regulation 1VAC20-60-30 (amended 2016) allows devices in polling places but does not mention ballot photos specifically; a 2016 AG opinion reportedly said voters may photograph their own ballots (not opened on oag.state.va.us).

polls.open: Voting centers open 18 days before Election Day
polls.summary: Washington votes by mail. Put your ballot in an official drop box by 8 p.m. on Election Day, or mail it with a postmark dated on or before Election Day; mailing a week early is recommended. Voting centers stay open until 8 p.m.
polls.quote: each ballot bearing a postmark on or before the date of the special election, general election, primary, or presidential primary and received no later than the day before certification, must be included in the canvass report.

id.summary: Washington votes by mail and checks signatures rather than ID. At a voting center, staff compare your signature or check ID before you use an accessible voting unit.
id.quote: The county auditor must either compare the voter’s signature or check identification before voters may use these units.

registration.deadline: Online and mail registrations must be received by Monday, October 26, 2026 (8 days before). In person at a county elections office or voting center until 8 p.m. on Election Day, November 3, 2026.
registration.summary: Register online or by mail so it arrives by October 26, 2026. You can register in person until 8 p.m. on Election Day.
registration.quote: You can register in person until 8 p.m. on Election Day to participate in that election.

selfie.summary: Washington does not directly prohibit ballot selfies. It is illegal to view someone else's ballot for a purpose such as vote buying.
selfie.quote: The state of Washington does not directly prohibit ballot selfies. However, it is illegal to view another’s ballot for a purpose prohibited by law, such as vote buying.

WA.notes: Drop box rule quote (SOS FAQ): 'Return your ballot to an official ballot drop box by 8 p.m. on Election Day.' SOS recommends mailing more than a week before Election Day because late-postmarked ballots cannot be counted. RCW 29A.60.190 amendment history ends 2019 on the page fetched. Oct 26 date is from the SOS registration page's Dates & Deadlines block.

polls.summary: Polls are open 6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. on Election Day at your assigned polling place.
polls.quote: When and where do I vote? Election Day: 6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. at your polling place.

id.summary: You must show an unexpired photo ID, such as a WV driver's license, U.S. passport, or WV student ID. Without one, you vote provisionally and show ID before canvass.
id.quote: West Virginia voters must show an approved form of photo identification at the polls during early voting or on Election Day. All forms of ID must be valid and not expired.

registration.deadline: Tuesday, October 13, 2026 (21 days before the election).
registration.summary: The registration deadline for the November 3 election was October 13, 2026. West Virginia has no Election Day registration.
registration.quote: October 13, 2026 — Voter Registration Deadline

selfie.summary: State law bars taking any recording or electronic device into the voting booth to record the voting process. No law found that addresses photos of a mail ballot.
selfie.quote: No person may enter a voting booth with any recording or electronic device in order to record or interfere with the voting process.

WV.notes: Photo ID changed recently: non-photo IDs (bank statements, utility bills, etc.) are no longer accepted for most voters (W.Va. Code 3-1-34 as now summarized by SOS). Exceptions: a poll worker who has known you 6+ months, or an adult who has known you 6+ months signs an affidavit and shows photo ID; care-facility residents. Registration deadline quote is from the 2026 General Election dates list on the GoVoteWV page. Selfie: a past SOS spokesperson told news outlets photographing any part of voting is illegal, but the statute only covers devices in the booth.

polls.summary: Polls are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Election Day, November 3, 2026. Absentee ballots must reach your municipal clerk by 8 p.m. on Election Day.
polls.quote: November 3, 2026 - from 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. Register to Vote at Your Polling Place- Voters can register to vote at their polling place on Election Day, November 3, 2026.

id.summary: You must show an acceptable photo ID, such as a Wisconsin driver's license, free state ID card, or U.S. passport. Without one, you vote provisionally and must show ID afterward.
id.quote: WISCONSIN NOW REQUIRES A PHOTO ID TO VOTE

registration.deadline: Online and by mail (postmarked) by October 14, 2026; in person at your municipal clerk's office until 5 p.m. October 30, 2026; at your polling place on Election Day, November 3, 2026, with proof of residence.
registration.summary: Register online or by mail by October 14, at your clerk's office until 5 p.m. October 30, or at your polling place on Election Day. Bring proof of residence.
registration.quote: October 14, 2026- Deadline to Register by Mail - Your voter registration form, along with proof of residence must be postmarked to your municipal clerk no later than October 14, 2026.

selfie.summary: State law makes it an offense to show your marked ballot to anyone, which covers sharing a ballot selfie.
selfie.quote: Shows his or her marked ballot to any person or places a mark upon the ballot so it is identifiable as his or her ballot.

WI.notes: elections.wi.gov / bringit.wi.gov / myvote.wi.gov block curl; read in Chrome. Provisional-ballot follow-up (show ID to the clerk by 4 p.m. the Friday after the election) is general knowledge, not quoted; the summary says only 'must show ID afterward'. Accepted ID examples (driver's license, state ID, passport) are standard WI list items; the bringit page fetched mentions the driver license and free state ID. Selfie: Wis. Stat. 12.13(1)(f) listed under election fraud; WEC guidance on selfies not opened.

polls.summary: Polls are open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. If you are in line at 7 p.m., you can still vote. Absentee ballots must reach your county clerk by 7 p.m. on Election Day.
polls.quote: Polls are open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., or until the last person in line at 7 p.m. has voted.

id.summary: You must show an acceptable ID, such as a Wyoming driver's license or ID card, U.S. passport, tribal ID, or a valid Medicare or Medicaid card.
id.quote: Voters are required to show an acceptable form of identification when voting in person.

registration.deadline: Registration closes 14 days before the election (Tuesday, October 20, 2026), but you can register and vote at the same time during the absentee voting period or at your polling place on Election Day, November 3, 2026.
registration.summary: The regular deadline is 14 days before the election, October 20. You can still register and vote the same day during early absentee voting or on Election Day. Bring proof of identity, citizenship, and residency.
registration.quote: The deadline for voter registration is 14 days before an election. However, you may register and vote at the same time -- during the absentee voting period or on Election Day.

WY.notes: Voter ID law took effect 2022. Medicare/Medicaid cards (non-photo) are accepted for now; the SOS FAQ says they will no longer be accepted after December 31, 2029, so classed id_nonphoto. Poll hours also in W.S. 22-13-101 ('Polls shall be open at seven (7:00) a.m. and close at seven (7:00) p.m., local time'). Registration now requires proof of U.S. citizenship per the SOS registration page. Oct 20 computed from the 14-day rule. Selfie: no provision found in Title 22 (searched for photograph, exhibit, reveal, secrecy) and no SOS guidance found.
